title: Typed layer use cases
description: What an application developer does with the typed API, step by step, and the branches the code has. Steps the JSON layer runs are cited to src/ and described in its views.

entities.name: Create a date
entities.description: A developer makes a date from year, month and day, or from text, and learns why it can't exist when it can't (tasks a-date and feb-30 of docs/side-by-side.md).
entities.goal: Hold a value for a calendar day, or know exactly why the day doesn't exist.
preconditions: The developer's crate depends on utv.
postconditions: The developer holds a CivilDate that names a real proleptic Gregorian day, or a Diagnostics (or an Outcome) whose code says why there is none.

flow.action: Calls CivilDate::of(year, month, day), or CivilDate::parse(text) or text.parse::<CivilDate>().
Writes the fields as a canonical UTV civil date (for text, parse_text reads it).
Reads the value back with the JSON layer's reader: the month, the day in that year's month, and that its day number fits i128.

alternatives.condition: The month is not 1 to 12.
alternatives.outcome: Err with month-out-of-range (invalid).

alternatives.condition: The day doesn't exist in that month: 30 February, or 29 February in 2026 or 1900.
alternatives.outcome: Err with day-out-of-range (invalid) and a message such as 2026-02 has no day 30.

alternatives.condition: The year is so large that its day number leaves the i128 range.
alternatives.outcome: Err with implementation-limit (unsupported).

alternatives.condition: The text is not ISO 8601 extended date text.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::Invalid with syntax; a week or ordinal date or basic format is Outcome::Unsupported with unsupported-form.

alternatives.condition: The text is a valid value of another type, such as 2026-11.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::Invalid with kind-mismatch.

entities.name: Add months to a date
entities.description: A developer moves a date by months and decides what happens when the day doesn't exist in the target month (task month-end).
entities.goal: Move a date by whole months, and choose deliberately what 31 January + 1 month is.
preconditions: The developer holds a CivilDate (CivilDateTime and ZonedIntent have the same methods).
postconditions: The developer has the date in the target month, or Outcome::None with month-end and then the clamped date if they ask for it.

flow.action: Calls date.add_months(n), or add_years(n) or add(Period).
Writes the date and Period::months(n) as UTV JSON with the policy monthEnd reject, and calls the JSON layer's add, which adds years and months first.
Checks that the day exists in the resulting month, then adds weeks and days.
Returns Outcome::Unique with the new date.
Matches on the outcome; for a missing day, calls add_months_constrained(n) to clamp, or answers in their own way.

alternatives.condition: The day doesn't exist in the target month (31 January + 1 month).
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::None with month-end and a message such as 2026-02 has no day 31.

alternatives.condition: The developer asks for the constrained form.
alternatives.outcome: add_months_constrained clamps to the last day of the month (28 February 2026) and returns the date itself.

alternatives.condition: add(Period) on a CivilDate is given hours, minutes or seconds.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::Invalid with kind-mismatch.

alternatives.condition: The value is a ZonedIntent with an asserted offset.
alternatives.outcome: The zone is kept and the assertion dropped; Unique carries the info code offset-assertion-dropped.

entities.name: Resolve a wall time in a named zone
entities.description: A developer turns a wall time in an IANA zone into an instant under rules they loaded, including a wall time that never happened or happened twice (tasks meeting-in-paris, dst-gap, dst-overlap).
entities.goal: Know which instant a wall time in a zone is, or that there is none or more than one, under rules they chose.
preconditions: The developer has a zone rule bundle in the format of conformance/rules/demo-zones.json.
The wall time is a valid CivilDateTime.
postconditions: The developer has the instant, both instants of an overlap, or an outcome whose code says why there is no answer; the rules used are the ones in their TemporalContext.

flow.action: Loads the rules and builds a context: TemporalContext::with(ZoneRules::load(path)?).
Calls zoned.resolve(&ctx), or resolve_with(&ctx, policy) with a Gap and an Overlap.
Reads the wall time as if it were UTC (L), takes every offset in force within a day of L, and keeps t = L − o where the offset at t is o.
Applies an asserted offset first, then the gap and overlap policy to the candidates.

alternatives.condition: The file can't be read or isn't a rule bundle.
alternatives.outcome: Err with malformed-value.

alternatives.condition: The rules have no such zone.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::Unsupported with unknown-zone.

alternatives.condition: The wall time is less than a day inside the rules' validity window.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::Unsupported with outside-rule-window: rules are never extrapolated.

alternatives.condition: The value asserts an offset that no candidate has, including any assertion in a gap.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::Invalid with offset-mismatch, whatever the policy.

alternatives.condition: No candidate (a gap) under Gap::Reject or Gap::PreserveUnresolved.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::None with gap.

alternatives.condition: No candidate under Gap::ShiftForward.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::Unique with the wall time shifted forward by the gap (02:30 gives 03:30 EDT), and an info note gap.

alternatives.condition: Two candidates (an overlap) under Overlap::Reject or Overlap::All.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::Multiple with both instants, ascending; Reject adds the warning ambiguous.

alternatives.condition: Two candidates under Overlap::Earliest or Overlap::Latest.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::Unique with the earlier or the later instant.

entities.name: Compare two values
entities.description: A developer orders two values. Values whose order can't depend on zone rules compare with < and Ord; zoned intentions have no Ord, so `<` on them doesn't compile, and they compare through the context, which may answer that the order depends on an overlap (task compare-dates). At the JSON layer, compare refuses zoned values with needs-zone-rules.
entities.goal: Know which of two values comes first, or that the answer depends on which side of a DST overlap is meant.
preconditions: The developer holds two values of the same type; for zoned values, a TemporalContext with rules for their zones.
postconditions: The developer has an Ordering, or an outcome listing the possible orders or saying why there is none.

flow.action: Asks for the order: a < b or a.cmp(&b) for a type with Ord; ctx.compare(&a, &b) for two ZonedIntents.
Resolves both values under ResolutionPolicy::STRICT and keeps every candidate instant and every diagnostic.
Compares every candidate of one with every candidate of the other, and keeps the distinct orders.
Returns Outcome::Unique(Ordering) when there is one order.

alternatives.condition: Both values are of a type with Ord: dates, year-months, times, date-times, fixed-offset date-times or instants.
alternatives.outcome: The Ordering itself, with no Outcome: civil values by their fields (a missing second as 0, then 09:30 before 09:30:00), fixed-offset date-times by instant, instants exactly.

alternatives.condition: The order depends on which side of an overlap is meant, such as 01:30 against 01:45 on 1 November 2026 in New York.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome::Multiple with the possible orders, ascending, keeping ambiguous.

alternatives.condition: Either value can't be resolved.
alternatives.outcome: That resolution's outcome: None (gap), Unsupported (unknown-zone, outside-rule-window) or Invalid (offset-mismatch).

relatedViews.relationship: The capabilities these use cases use.
Month end and DST resolution, which the JSON-layer steps carry out.
The JSON-layer operations add, resolve and parse_text that the system steps run.
